details.claim: Liu Yan was a descendant of King Lu Gong.
evidence: Liu Yanchuan, Liu Yan, courtesy name Junlang, was from Jingling, Jiangxia, and was a descendant of King Lu Gong.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Yan served as a local official.
evidence: When Liu Yan was young, he served in prefectures and counties
was gradually promoted to Nanyang Prefect
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Yan served as Nanyang Prefect.
evidence: was gradually promoted to Nanyang Prefect
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Yan served as Zongzheng.
evidence: Later, he was recommended as a virtuous and upright person, and was gradually promoted to Nanyang Prefect, Zongzheng, and Taichang.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Yan served as Taichang.
evidence: Later, he was recommended as a virtuous and upright person, and was gradually promoted to Nanyang Prefect, Zongzheng, and Taichang.
details.label: supported

details.claim: During Emperor Ling's reign, rebellions spread due to weak governors.
evidence: At that time, Emperor Ling's political education was in decline and there were military rebellions everywhere. Liu Yan believed that the power of the governor was small and he had no ability to stop it, and the people he appointed were incompetent, so the rebellions often increased.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Yan proposed appointing powerful governors to control regions.
evidence: Liu Yan believed that the power of the governor was small and he had no ability to stop it, and the people he appointed were incompetent, so the rebellions often increased. So he suggested that the governor should be appointed to control one side and carefully select ministers who hold important positions as shepherds.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Yan's suggestion was initially ignored.
evidence: His suggestions were not implemented in time
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Liu Yan's suggestion was later adopted after several governors were killed.
evidence: His suggestions were not implemented in time, but Xi Jian, the governor of Yizhou, was disturbing the people with his administration. Rumors spread far and wide, and Zhang Yi, the governor of Bingzhou, and Geng Bi, the governor of Liangzhou, were both killed by bandits, so Liu Yan's proposal was adopted.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Yan was sent to lead Yizhou as shepherd.
evidence: Liu Yan was sent to serve as the envoy to supervise the army and lead the shepherd of Yizhou.
details.label: supported

details.claim: In Yizhou, Liu Yan faced a rebellion led by Ma Xiang.
evidence: At this time, Yizhou's thieves and horses also called themselves "Yellow Turbans", gathered thousands of people who were suffering from labor, first killed Mianzhu Ling, attacked Luo County, killed Xi Jian, and then attacked Shu County and Qianwei. Within a month, they captured and destroyed three counties.
Ma Xiang called himself the Son of Heaven and had a tribe of more than 100,000 people.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Ma Xiang claimed to be the Son of Heaven.
evidence: Ma Xiang called himself the Son of Heaven and had a tribe of more than 100,000 people.
details.label: supported

details.claim: The rebellion by Ma Xiang was suppressed by Jia Long.
evidence: Ma Xiang called himself the Son of Heaven and had a tribe of more than 100,000 people. Ma Xiang sent troops to conquer Bajun and killed Tangbu, the prefect of Bajun. Jia Long, a minister of Yizhou, originally led hundreds of soldiers to garrison in Jianwei, so he gathered the officials and people to attack Ma Xiang and defeated him.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Yan appointed Zhang Lu.
evidence: Liu Yan appointed Zhang Lu as the governor of the Sima.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Zhang Lu later seized Hanzhong.
evidence: Zhang Lu had occupied Hanzhong, so he killed Zhang Xiu and merged his troops.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Zhang Lu killed the prefect of Hanzhong.
evidence: Liu Yan appointed Zhang Lu as the governor of the Sima. He and other Sima Zhang Xiu led troops to kill Su Gu, the prefect of Hanzhong, by surprise.
details.label: partially_supported

details.claim: Liu Yan grew arrogant.
evidence: From then on, Liu Yan's spirit gradually became stronger and stronger, and he built the emperor's carriage and more than a thousand baggage vehicles.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Liu Yan built imperial carriages.
evidence: From then on, Liu Yan's spirit gradually became stronger and stronger, and he built the emperor's carriage and more than a thousand baggage vehicles.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Yan killed powerful locals.
evidence: Liu Yan wanted to achieve his arrogance by establishing strict criminal laws, so he used other things as an excuse to kill more than a dozen powerful people in the state, which made the scholars and the people complain.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Yan's actions caused resentment.
evidence: Liu Yan wanted to achieve his arrogance by establishing strict criminal laws, so he used other things as an excuse to kill more than a dozen powerful people in the state, which made the scholars and the people complain.
From then on, Liu Yan's spirit gradually became stronger and stronger, and he built the emperor's carriage and more than a thousand baggage vehicles.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Yan lost two sons in a failed plot.
evidence: In the first year of Xingping, General Ma Teng and Liu Fan discussed killing Li Cui. Liu Yan sent 5,000 Shu soldiers to help, but they were defeated. Liu Fan and Liu Dan were both killed.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Yan died of illness.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Liu Yan's son Liu Zhang succeeded him.
evidence: Liu Yan had four sons, Liu Fan served as Zuo Zhonglang, Liu Dan served as the censor of the book, and Liu Zhang served as the captain of Fengche. They all followed Emperor Xian in Chang'an, and only Liu Mao, the commander of another department, followed Liu Yan in Yizhou.
The senior officials in Yizhou, such as Tanti and others, coveted Liu Zhang's gentleness and kindness and appointed him as the governor.
The emperor issued an edict and appointed Liu Zhang as the envoy to supervise the army and lead the herdsman of Yizhou, and appointed Chang Wei as the general of Zhengshu Zhonglang.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Zhang lacked authority.
evidence: Liu Zhang has a weak and tolerant temperament and lacks authority and strategy.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Zhang's rule led to internal strife and rebellion.
evidence: Liu Zhang has a weak and tolerant temperament and lacks authority and strategy. The invasion of Shuzhou was violent and became a disaster for the people. Liu Zhang was unable to stop it. The old scholars complained and rebelled.

Seeing the discord among the people, Zhao Wei secretly colluded with the prominent families in the state. In the fifth year of Jian'an, Zhao Wei turned his forces to jointly attack Liu Zhang. Shu County, Guanghan, and Qianwei all betrayed Liu Zhang and responded.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Zhang surrendered to Liu Bei after a siege.
evidence: In the 19th year, Liu Bei marched and surrounded Chengdu for dozens of days. There were 30,000 elite troops in the city with enough food to last for a year. The officials and the people wanted to resist. Liu Zhang said: My father and son have been in Yizhou for more than 20 years. They have not shown any kindness to the people, but they have fought for three years. Many people died in the wilderness, just because of me. How can I feel at ease! So he opened the city gate and went out to surrender.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Liu Zhang died later.
evidence: Later Liu Zhang died of illness.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu was the son of Sikong Yuan Feng.
evidence: Yuan Shu, courtesy name Gongdao, was born in Ruyang, Runan, and was the son of Sikong Yuan Feng.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu was known for chivalry.
evidence: When he was young, he was famous for his chivalrous spirit, and he often went hunting with his young master buddies.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Yuan Shu later changed from being chivalrous.
evidence: When he was young, he was famous for his chivalrous spirit, and he often went hunting with his young master buddies. Later, he changed a lot.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu fled to Nanyang after Dong Zhuo's coup.
evidence: At that time, Dong Zhuo was preparing to change his position as emperor and appointed Yuan Shu as the post-general. Yuan Shu was afraid of being involved in Dong Zhuo's troubles and ran to Nanyang.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu allied with Sun Jian.
evidence: It happened that Sun Jian, the governor of Changsha, killed Zhang Zi, the governor of Nanyang, and led his troops to obey Yuan Shu.
Yuan Shu also wrote a letter recommending Sun Jian to be the governor of Yuzhou. Sun Jian was asked to lead the troops in Jingzhou and Yuzhou and defeated Dong Zhuo in Yangren.
In the third year of Chuping, Yuan Shu sent Sun Jian to attack Liu Biao in Xiangyang, and Sun Jian died in the battle.
When he heard that Sun Jian had obtained the imperial seal, he imprisoned Sun Jian's wife to obtain the imperial seal.
After Bai Sunjian's death, his son Sun Ce took command of Sun Jian's men. Yuan Shu sent Sun Ce to attack Liu Yao, the governor of Yangzhou, and defeated Liu Yao.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Conflicts arose between Yuan Shu and his cousin Yuan Shao over leadership.
evidence: Yuan Shu's cousin Yuan Shao took advantage of the fact that Sun Jian had not returned from his crusade against Dong Zhuo and was far away, so he sent his general Zhou Xin to capture Sun Jian's Yuzhou. Yuan Shu was very angry and beat Zhou Xin away.

Yuan Shao discussed making Liu Yu the emperor, but Yuan Shu liked to indulge and was afraid of making an older person emperor, so he refused to agree on the grounds of public opinion. When they got together, there was a gap between the two.
So the two of them each made friends as foreign aid to influence each other's ideas. Yuan Shu befriended Gongsun Zan, while Yuan Shao allied with Liu Biao.
Most of the heroes attached themselves to Yuan Shao. Yuan Shu got angry and said: 'Are these princes not following me, but following my servants?'
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu declared himself emperor in 197 CE.
evidence: In the second year of Jian'an, Yuan Shu used the talisman made up by Zhang Jiong from Hanoi to finally assume his name and call himself the "Zhong Family".
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu cited prophecies for his claim.
evidence: When Yuan Shu was young, he saw a prophecy book that said that the one who replaced the Han Dynasty would be Dang Tu Gao, which meant that his name matched the prophecy book.

And because the Yuan family came from the state of Chen, they were descendants of Shun. Replacing red virtue with yellow virtue is in line with the order of operation of the five virtues, so he has the idea of ​​​​transgression and rebellion.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu cited his family's lineage for his claim.
evidence: And because the Yuan family came from the state of Chen, they were descendants of Shun.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Yuan Shu's rule was marked by extravagance.
evidence: However, he did not pay attention to regulating the legal system. He relied on plundering to save money, was extravagant and indulgent, and was greedy.

When the name was stolen, the debauchery and extravagance became increasingly serious. He had hundreds of concubines, all of whom were wearing silk clothes and eating delicacies. However, while his subordinates were hungry and poor, he never cared about them.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu's rule was marked by cruelty.
evidence: he did not pay attention to regulating the legal system. He relied on plundering to save money, was extravagant and indulgent, and was greedy. The people were disgusted with him.

the debauchery and extravagance became increasingly serious. He had hundreds of concubines, all of whom were wearing silk clothes and eating delicacies. However, while his subordinates were hungry and poor, he never cared about them.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Yuan Shu's rule led to widespread discontent.
evidence: However, he did not pay attention to regulating the legal system. He relied on plundering to save money, was extravagant and indulgent, and was greedy. The people were disgusted with him.

Yuan Shu's army was weak, his main generals died, and everyone rebelled. Coupled with drought and poor harvests, the scholars and people suffered from hunger and cold, and the food along the Yangtze and Huaihe Rivers was almost exhausted.

When the name was stolen, the debauchery and extravagance became increasingly serious. He had hundreds of concubines, all of whom were wearing silk clothes and eating delicacies. However, while his subordinates were hungry and poor, he never cared about them.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu was defeated by Cao Cao.
evidence: Cao Cao then personally conquered Yuan Shu.
Cao Cao defeated the two men and killed Qiao Rui.
Yuan Shu's army was weak, his main generals died, and everyone rebelled.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu was defeated by Lu Bu.
evidence: Yuan Shu was angry that Lu Bu had killed Han Yin, so he sent his generals Zhang Xun, Qiao Rui and others to cooperate with Han Xian and Yang Feng, leading tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to attack Lu Bu in seven directions.

Han Xian and Yang Feng were very happy, so they attacked Zhang Xun and others in Xiapi and captured Qiao Rui alive. The rest of the troops fled. Many people were killed and wounded, fell into the water and drowned, and almost the entire army was wiped out.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu's army weakened after defeats.
evidence: Yuan Shu's army was weak, his main generals died, and everyone rebelled.
Cao Cao defeated the two men and killed Qiao Rui. Zhang Xun retreated and fled.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu died in 199 CE.
evidence: In the summer of the fourth year of Jian'an, Yuan Shu burned the palace and went to his subordinates Chen Jian and Lei Bo in Qianshan. He was rejected by Chen Jian and others. Finally, he was very poor and distressed, and the soldiers broke up and fled. Yuan Shu was sad and angry, and didn't know what to do, so he gave the title to Yuan Shao and said: ... In June, we arrived at Jiangting. Yuan Shu sat on the bamboo bed and sighed and said: Is this what Yuan Shu has done? Yuan Shu became ill due to his anger, vomited blood and died.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu died vomiting blood in despair.
evidence: Yuan Shu became ill due to his anger, vomited blood and died.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yuan Shu's family sought refuge with Sun Ce.
evidence: His wife and children took refuge with Yuan Shu's former subordinate Liu Xun, the governor of Lujiang. Sun Ce defeated Liu Xun, and they were taken in and taken care of by Sun Ce.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Lu Bu was a skilled warrior from Wuyuan.
evidence: Lu Bu, courtesy name Fengxian, was a native of Wuyuan and Jiuyuan.
Because of his strong martial arts skills and bravery in combat, he served in Bingzhou.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu served under Ding Yuan.
evidence: The governor Ding Yuan served as the cavalry captain and was stationed in Hanoi. He appointed Lu Bu as chief administrator and was very close to him.
When He Jin was defeated, Dong Zhuo lured Lu Bu to kill Ding Yuan and annex his troops.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu killed Ding Yuan to join Dong Zhuo.
evidence: When Emperor Ling died, Ding Yuan was summoned by He Jin and led his army to Luoyang to serve as Jinwu. When He Jin was defeated, Dong Zhuo lured Lu Bu to kill Ding Yuan and annex his troops.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu later killed Dong Zhuo with Wang Yun's persuasion.
evidence: Lu Bu agreed to Wang Yun and stabbed Dong Zhuo to death at the gate of Hemen.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu fled after Li Cui's attack.
evidence: Lu Bu failed in the battle with Li Cui, so he led hundreds of cavalry, tied Dong Zhuo's head to the saddle, escaped from Wuguan, and rushed to Nanyang.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu allied with various warlords.
evidence: Lu Bu defected to Yuan Shu. Yuan Shu treated Lu Bu very well
Lu Bu left Yuan Shu and went to Hanoi to join Zhang Yang
Lu Bu defected to Yuan Shao. Yuan Shao and Lu Bu attacked Zhang Yan in Changshan
Zhang Miao, his younger brother Zhang Chao, Chen Gong and others welcomed Lu Bu and asked him to be the herdsman of Yanzhou
Lu Bu fled to Liu Bei
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu allied with Yuan Shu.
evidence: Yuan Shu wanted to unite with Lu Bu to attack Liu Bei, so he wrote to Lu Bu
Yuan Shu was afraid that Lü Bu would harm him and proposed marriage for his son, but Lü Bu agreed again.
Yuan Shu sent Han Yin to tell Lü Bu about the arrogance and asked to take his daughter-in-law away. Lü Bu asked his daughter to go with Han Yin.
In the third year of Jian'an, Lu Bu finally defected to Yuan Shu and sent Gao Shun to attack Liu Bei in Peixian County and defeated Liu Bei.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu allied with Liu Bei.
evidence: Lu Bu was angry that Yuan Shu stopped bringing grain, so he prepared chariots and horses to welcome Liu Bei, appointed Liu Bei as the governor of Yuzhou, and sent him to garrison Xiaopei.
Lu Bu said to Ji Ling: Xuande is my brother.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu frequently betrayed his allies.
evidence: Dong Zhuo lured Lü Bu to kill Ding Yuan and annex his troops.
Lu Bu agreed to Wang Yun and stabbed Dong Zhuo to death at the gate of Hemen.

Yuan Shu treated Lu Bu very well, and Lu Bu relied on himself to kill Dong Zhuo. If you are kind to the Yuan family, you will indulge your subordinates in looting. Yuan Shu had a headache, and Lu Bu felt uneasy, so he left Yuan Shu and went to Hanoi to join Zhang Yang.

Lu Bu defected to Yuan Shao. ... Lu Bu relied on his military exploits and once again asked Yuan Shao to increase his army, but Yuan Shao refused. ... Lu Bu felt uneasy and asked to return to Luoyang.

Lu Bu was angry that Yuan Shu had killed Han Yin, so he sent his generals Zhang Xun, Qiao Rui and others to cooperate with Han Xian and Yang Feng, leading tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to attack Lu Bu in seven directions.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu was known for his prowess.
evidence: Because of his strong martial arts skills and bravery in combat, he served in Bingzhou.

Lu Bu often rode a good horse named Red Rabbit that could leap over city walls and fly across trenches. He and his fierce generals Cheng Lian, Wei Yue and dozens of others rode to attack Zhang Yan's military formation. Sometimes they went three or four times a day and came back each time with the enemy's heads chopped off.
Lu Bu is a fierce warrior, good at fighting, and brave and invincible.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu defeated Zhang Yan.
evidence: Yuan Shao and Lu Bu attacked Zhang Yan in Changshan. Zhang Yan had more than 10,000 elite soldiers and several thousand cavalry. Lu Bu often rode a good horse named Red Rabbit that could leap over city walls and fly across trenches. He and his fierce generals Cheng Lian, Wei Yue and dozens of others rode to attack Zhang Yan's military formation. Sometimes they went three or four times a day and came back each time with the enemy's heads chopped off. After fighting for more than ten days, Zhang Yan's army was finally defeated.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu alienated allies due to his brutality.
evidence: Lu Bu relied on his military exploits and once again asked Yuan Shao to increase his army, but Yuan Shao refused. Most of Lu Bu's generals and soldiers were vicious and brutal, which gave Yuan Shao a headache.

Yuan Shu treated Lu Bu very well, and Lu Bu relied on himself to kill Dong Zhuo. If you are kind to the Yuan family, you will indulge your subordinates in looting. Yuan Shu had a headache, and Lu Bu felt uneasy, so he left Yuan Shu and went to Hanoi to join Zhang Yang.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu surrendered to Cao Cao after a siege at Xiapi.
evidence: Cao Cao then personally led his troops to attack Lu Bu, and the troops arrived at Xiapi City.
Lu Bu saw Cao Cao and said: From now on, the world will be peaceful.
Lu Bu said: There is no one you worry about more than me, Lu Bu. I have surrendered now.
Lu Bu, Chen Gong and Gao Shunquan were strangled to death, and their heads were sent to the Xu County market for public display.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu was executed along with his generals Chen Gong and Gao Shun.
evidence: Lu Bu, Chen Gong and Gao Shunquan were strangled to death, and their heads were sent to the Xu County market for public display.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu's life was marked by shifting loyalties.
evidence: Dong Zhuo lured Lü Bu to kill Ding Yuan and annex his troops.
Lü Bu once made Dong Zhuo unhappy, so Dong Zhuo pulled out a small halberd and threw it at Lü Bu.
Lu Bu agreed to Wang Yun and stabbed Dong Zhuo to death at the gate of Hemen.
Lu Bu defected to Yuan Shao.
Lu Bu surrendered to Cao Cao.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Lu Bu's life was marked by ultimate failure.
evidence: Lu Bu failed in the battle with Li Cui, so he led hundreds of cavalry, tied Dong Zhuo's head to the saddle, escaped from Wuguan, and rushed to Nanyang.
Lu Bu was angry that Yuan Shu stopped bringing grain, so he prepared chariots and horses to welcome Liu Bei, appointed Liu Bei as the governor of Yuzhou, and sent him to garrison Xiaopei.

Lu Bu and his men boarded the Baimen Tower. As the soldiers surrounded him tightly, Lu Bu asked those around him to cut off his head and go to see Cao Cao. The people around him couldn't bear it, so they went downstairs to surrender.
Lu Bu, Chen Gong and Gao Shunquan were strangled to death, and their heads were sent to the Xu County market for public display.
Zan said: ... Yuan Shu was incompetent and greedy, and Lu Bu also failed.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju is a descendant of Tian Wan.
evidence: Sima Ranju is a descendant of Tian Wan.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Yan Ying recommended Sima Ranju to Qi Jinggong.
evidence: Yan Ying recommended Tian Rangju to Qi Jinggong, saying: Although Rangju is the bastard of the Tian family, his literary talent can make everyone join him; his military strategy can make the enemy fear him. I hope the king can give him a try.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Jin and Yan attacked Qi.
evidence: During the period of Qi Jinggong, the Jin State sent troops to attack Qi State's Dong'a and Zhencheng, and the Yan State invaded Qi State's territory on the south bank of the Yellow River.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju had humble status.
evidence: Rangju said: "I am of a humble status. The king promoted me from the common people and placed me above the officials."
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju had literary and military talents.
evidence: Although Rangju is the bastard of the Tian family, his literary talent can make everyone join him; his military strategy can make the enemy fear him.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Qi Jinggong appointed Sima Ranju as general.
evidence: So Qi Jinggong summoned Rangju and discussed military and state affairs with him. After discussing with him, Qi Jinggong was very happy and immediately appointed him as a general and ordered him to lead troops to resist the armies of Yan and Jin.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju requested Zhuang Jia to supervise the army.
evidence: Rangju said: "I am of a humble status. The king promoted me from the common people and placed me above the officials. The soldiers will not obey and the people will not trust me. If a person has little qualifications, authority cannot be established. I hope the king can send a minister who is favored by the king and respected by the people to supervise the army. That will be enough."
So Qi Jinggong agreed to his request and sent Zhuang Jia to supervise the army.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Zhuang Jia was a trusted minister.
evidence: I hope the king can send a minister who is favored by the king and respected by the people to supervise the army.
So Qi Jinggong agreed to his request and sent Zhuang Jia to supervise the army.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju and Zhuang Jia agreed to meet at the camp gate at noon.
evidence: After Rang Ju bid farewell to Jinggong, she made an agreement with Zhuang Jia: "We will meet at the camp gate at noon tomorrow."
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju arrived early and set up timing devices.
evidence: The next day, Rang Ju rushed to the military gate first and set up a wooden watch and a clepsydra to wait for Zhuang Jia.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Zhuang Jia was delayed by farewell feasts.
evidence: Zhuang Jia has always been arrogant and dignified. He thinks that he is leading his own army and he is the supervisor of the army, so he is not particularly anxious. His relatives and friends bid farewell to him and invited him to drink wine.
Zhuang Jia apologized and explained: My friends and relatives sent me off, so I was delayed.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Zhuang Jia arrived at dusk.
evidence: By the time he finished his deployment, it was already dusk when Zhuang Jia arrived.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju condemned Zhuang Jia's lateness.
evidence: Rangju said: Why are you late even if you agree on the time?
So he called the military judge and asked: According to military law, what is said about people who are late for the agreed time? The answer was: He should be beheaded.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Sima Ranju said a general must forsake family, friendships, and personal safety in war.
evidence: Rangju said: As a general, you should forget about your family from the moment you receive an order. When you come to the army and issue the prescribed orders, you should forget about personal friendships. When you beat the drum and march, you should forget about your own life when the battle is urgent.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju executed Zhuang Jia under military law.
evidence: Rangju said: Why are you late even if you agree on the time?
So he called the military judge and asked: According to military law, what is said about people who are late for the agreed time? The answer was: He should be beheaded.
Not long after the messenger left, but before he could return, Zhuang Jia was beheaded and paraded in front of the three armies.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: The army was shocked by the execution.
evidence: Zhuang Jia was beheaded and paraded in front of the three armies. The entire army was shocked and frightened.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Qi Jinggong's envoy arrived with a pardon.
evidence: After a long time, the envoy sent by Qi Jinggong came to pardon Zhuang Jia with the festival talisman.
details.label: supported

details.claim: The envoy raced into camp.
evidence: The carriages and horses galloped straight into the military camp.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju declared that generals in the field need not accept all royal orders.
evidence: Rangju said: "Generals are in the army, and they do not have to accept some of the king's orders."
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju executed the envoy's servants and horses.
evidence: So he beheaded the servants of the messenger, cut off the wooden carriage on the left side, killed the horses driving the carriage on the left side, and paraded in front of the three armies.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju paraded the executed servants and horses before the troops.
evidence: So he beheaded the servants of the messenger, cut off the wooden carriage on the left side, killed the horses driving the carriage on the left side, and paraded in front of the three armies.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju personally cared for soldiers.
evidence: The native soldiers set up camp, dug wells and set up stoves, drank water and ate food, inquired about diseases, and arranged medicine. Tian Rangju personally checked and cared for them.
He also used all the supplies and food he had as a general to entertain the soldiers. He and the soldiers shared the food equally.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju shared provisions with soldiers.
evidence: He also used all the supplies and food he had as a general to entertain the soldiers. He and the soldiers shared the food equally.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju tended to the sick.
evidence: He also used all the supplies and food he had as a general to entertain the soldiers. He and the soldiers shared the food equally. Count up the weak and sick.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: After three days, the army was revitalized.
evidence: Three days later, the army was reorganized and prepared for battle.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: The Jin forces withdrew upon learning of this discipline.
evidence: When the Jin army learned of this situation, they withdrew their troops.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: The Yan forces withdrew upon learning of this discipline.
evidence: The Yan army knew about this situation and was dispersed as it retreated northward across the Yellow River.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Qi reclaimed lost territory.
evidence: The Qi army took advantage of the situation to pursue them, regained all the fallen territory, and then led its troops in triumph.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Sima Ranju returned in triumph.
evidence: The Qi army took advantage of the situation to pursue them, regained all the fallen territory, and then led its troops in triumph.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Qi Jinggong appointed Sima Ranju as Grand Sima.
evidence: Duke Jinggong of Qi met Tian Ranju and appointed him as Grand Sima with great respect and admiration.
details.label: supported

details.claim: The appointment elevated the Tian family's status.
evidence: Duke Jinggong of Qi met Tian Ranju and appointed him as Grand Sima with great respect and admiration. From then on, Tian's status in Qi State became more and more prominent day by day.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Officials Bao, Gao, and Guo slandered Sima Ranju.

details.claim: Sima Ranju was dismissed.
evidence: Qi Jinggong dismissed him from his official position, and Rangju died of illness soon after.

details.claim: Sima Ranju died from illness.
evidence: Qi Jinggong dismissed him from his official position, and Rangju died of illness soon after.

details.claim: The Tian family later retaliated.

After that, when Tian Chang killed Duke Jian of Qi, he killed all the Gao and Guo families.

details.claim: The Tian family killed the Gao and Guo clans.
evidence: Tian Qi, Tian Bao and others therefore resented the people of the Gao and Guo families.
After that, when Tian Chang killed Duke Jian of Qi, he killed all the Gao and Guo families.

evidence: When Tian Chang's great-grandson Tian He arrived, he established himself as king and was named King Qi Wei. When he led his troops in battles and exercised his authority, he widely imitated Rang Ju's methods, and princes from all over the world came to Qi to pay homage.

details.claim: King Qi Wei incorporated Sima Ranju's strategies into the 'Sima's Art of War'.

details.claim: Dou Ying was the Marquis of Weiqi.
evidence: After all the rebellions in the seven countries were put down, the emperor granted Dou Ying the title of Marquis of Wei.

During the reign of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, every time the court discussed major military and political affairs, all the princes did not dare to sit on an equal footing with Zhou Yafu, the Marquis of Tiao, and Dou Ying, the Marquis of Wei Qi.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Dou Ying was a relative of Empress Dowager Dou.
evidence: Wei Qihou Dou Ying was the son of the cousin of Empress Dou, Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Dou Ying served as the Prime Minister of Wu.
evidence: During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Dou Ying served as the Prime Minister of Wu State
details.label: supported

details.claim: Dou Ying was dismissed due to illness.
evidence: During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Dou Ying served as the Prime Minister of Wu State, but was dismissed due to illness.
details.label: supported

details.claim: During Emperor Jing's reign, Dou Ying opposed the emperor's suggestion to pass the throne to his brother, King Xiao of Liang.
evidence: At this time, Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty said casually: After my death, I will pass the throne to King Liang.

At this time, Dou Ying offered a glass of wine to the emperor and said: The world was created by Emperor Gaozu, and the throne should be passed down from father to son. This is the system established by the Han Dynasty. Why should the emperor pass it on to King Liang without authorization?
details.label: supported

details.claim: Dou Ying angered Empress Dowager Dou by opposing the throne succession.
evidence: At this time, Dou Ying offered a glass of wine to the emperor and said: The world was created by Emperor Gaozu, and the throne should be passed down from father to son. This is the system established by the Han Dynasty. Why should the emperor pass it on to King Liang without authorization?
Queen Mother Dou hated Dou Ying for this reason.
details.label: supported

details.claim: When the seven kingdoms rebelled, Emperor Jing appointed Dou Ying as a general.
evidence: In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign in the Han Dynasty, seven kingdoms including Wu and Chu rebelled. The emperor found that no one in the royal family or anyone with the surname Dou was as capable as Dou Ying, so he summoned Dou Ying.
So he appointed Dou Ying as the general and rewarded him with a thousand catties of gold.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Dou Ying recommended talented men.
evidence: At this time, Yuan Ang, Luan Bu and other famous generals and wise men retired from their posts and stayed at home, so Dou Ying recommended them to the emperor.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Dou Ying distributed his gold reward to subordinates.
evidence: The gold rewarded by the emperor was all displayed in the corridor. When the subordinate officers passed by, they were allowed to use it as they saw fit. None of the gold rewarded by the emperor was taken home.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Dou Ying successfully suppressed the rebellion.
evidence: After all the rebellions in the seven countries were put down, the emperor granted Dou Ying the title of Marquis of Wei.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Dou Ying earned the title of Marquis of Weiqi.
evidence: After all the rebellions in the seven countries were put down, the emperor granted Dou Ying the title of Marquis of Wei.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Dou Ying served as the tutor of Prince Li.
evidence: In the fourth year of Emperor Jing's reign in the Han Dynasty, he established Prince Li and appointed Wei Qihou as his tutor.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Dou Ying was deposed after arguing for the prince.
evidence: In the seventh year of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Prince Li was deposed. Wei Qihou argued for Prince Li many times, but to no avail.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Dou Ying retired.
evidence: Dou Ying also felt that Zhan Shi's official position was too small, so he resigned on the pretext of illness.
Wei Qihou pretended to be ill and lived in seclusion at the foot of Nanshan Mountain in Lantian County for several months.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Dou Ying was persuaded to return to court.
evidence: Wei Qihou pretended to be ill and lived in seclusion at the foot of Nanshan Mountain in Lantian County for several months. Many guests and debaters came to persuade him, but no one could persuade him to return to the capital.
Gao Sui, a native of Liang, came to persuade Wei Qihou and said: ... Wei Qihou thought he was right, so he went back to the court and met the emperor as before.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Empress Dowager Dou recommended Dou Ying for prime minister.
evidence: When Taohou Liu She was dismissed from the post of prime minister, Empress Dowager Dou recommended Wei Qihou to be prime minister many times.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Emperor Jing refused to make Dou Ying prime minister.
evidence: Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty said: Does the Queen Mother think that I am stingy in not letting Wei Qihou become prime minister? Wei Qihou is a proud and complacent person, prone to self-admiration, careless and frivolous in doing things, making it difficult for him to serve as prime minister and assume important responsibilities. Finally, he was not appointed, and Wei Wan, Marquis of Jianling, was appointed as prime minister.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Emperor Jing cited Dou Ying's arrogance as the reason for refusal.
evidence: Wei Qihou is a proud and complacent person, prone to self-admiration, careless and frivolous in doing things, making it difficult for him to serve as prime minister and assume important responsibilities.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Tian Fen was the Marquis of Wu'an.
evidence: Tianfen, Marquis of Wu'an, was the half-brother of Emperor Jing and Queen of the Han Dynasty.

Tian Fu and his younger brother Tian Sheng were both named Marquis of Wu'an and Marquis of Zhou Yang respectively in the same year that Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty died because they were the younger brothers of the Queen Mother.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen was the half-brother of Emperor Jing's queen.
evidence: Tianfen, Marquis of Wu'an, was the half-brother of Emperor Jing and Queen of the Han Dynasty.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen was initially humble.
evidence: After Wei Qihou became a general, when he was at the height of his prominence, Tian Fu was still an official, not a distinguished person. He went to and from Wei Qihou's home, attended banquets, knelt down and stood up like Wei Qihou's descendants.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen rose to prominence after Emperor Jing's death.
evidence: When Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty passed away, the prince ascended the throne and the Queen Mother became regent. Her suppression and appeasement actions throughout the country mostly adopted the strategy of Tian Fu's guests. Tian Fu and his younger brother Tian Sheng were both named Marquis of Wu'an and Marquis of Zhou Yang respectively in the same year that Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty died because they were the younger brothers of the Queen Mother.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen became a favored official.
evidence: Tianfen, Marquis of Wu'an, was the half-brother of Emperor Jing and Queen of the Han Dynasty. He was born in Changling.
In the later years of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Tian Fu also became prominent, favored and became a Taizhong doctor.
Tian Fu was eloquent and eloquent. He had studied books such as "Pan Yu" and the Queen Mother thought he had talent.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen became prime minister.
evidence: So Wu'an Hou Tianfan was appointed as the prime minister
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen became Taiwei.
evidence: appointed Marquis Wei Qi as prime minister and Marquis Wu'an as Taiwei.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen promoted Confucianism.
evidence: Dou Ying, the Marquis of Wei Qi, and Tian Fu, the Marquis of Wu'an, both loved Confucianism.
Empress Dowager Dou liked Huang Lao's theory, but Wei Qihou, Wu'anhou, Zhao Wan, Wang Zang and others tried hard to promote Confucianism and belittle Taoist theory.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen clashed with Empress Dowager Dou's preference for Taoism.
evidence: Empress Dowager Dou liked Huang Lao's theory, but Wei Qihou, Wu'anhou, Zhao Wan, Wang Zang and others tried hard to promote Confucianism and belittle Taoist theory.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: After Empress Dowager Dou's death, Tian Fen became prime minister.
evidence: In the sixth year of Jianyuan's reign, Empress Dowager Dou passed away. Prime Minister Xuchang and Yushi doctor Zhuang Qingzhai were dismissed from office because of poor funeral arrangements. So Wu'an Hou Tianfan was appointed as the prime minister
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen grew arrogant and powerful.
evidence: Marquis Wu'an became more arrogant day by day.
From then on, Marquis Wu'an became even more arrogant.
Marquis Wu'an was short in stature and unattractive in appearance, but he was very noble right from birth.

He also thought that the princes and kings at that time were all old, and the emperor had just ascended the throne and was very young. He served as the emperor's closest relative and confidant as the prime minister of the court. If he didn't rectify them severely and use etiquette to make them submit, the people of the world would not be obedient.

At that time, when the prime minister came to the court to perform affairs, he would often sit there for most of the day. The emperor would listen to what he said. Some of the people he recommended were promoted from idle residence to two thousand stone levels at once, transferring the emperor's power to his own hands.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen built lavish residences.
evidence: He built residences whose scale and luxury surpassed all the noble houses.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen accumulated wealth.
evidence: The fields and manors were extremely fertile, and there was an endless stream of people he sent to various counties to buy utensils on the road.
The princes presented him with countless treasures, gold, jade, dogs, horses, and playthings.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Dou Ying lost influence.
evidence: Since Wei Qihou lost Empress Dowager Dou, he was further alienated by the emperor and was not reused. He had no power. All the guests gradually left of their own accord, and even became lazy and arrogant towards him.
When Wei Qihou lost power, he also wanted to follow Guan Fu to take revenge on those who usually admired him but abandoned him after losing power.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Dou Ying was alienated.
evidence: Since Wei Qihou lost Empress Dowager Dou, he was further alienated by the emperor and was not reused.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Guan Fu was a brave general.
evidence: Guan Fu put on his armor and held a halberd in his hand, and summoned dozens of warriors in the army who had always been friendly with him and were willing to go with him. After walking out of the military gate, no one dared to move forward. Only the two of them and Guan Fu's slaves, a total of more than ten cavalry, rushed into the Wu army until they reached the Wu army's general flag, killing and wounding dozens of enemy soldiers.
Guan Fu suffered more than ten serious injuries on his body, but he happened to have precious medicine, so he survived.
When the Wu army was defeated, Guan Fu became famous all over the world.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Guan Fu gained fame during the seven kingdoms' rebellion.
evidence: During the rebellion of Wu and Chu, Yingyin Marquis Guan He served as a general and was a subordinate of Taiwei Zhou Yafu. He recommended Guan Meng to the Taiwei as a school captain.
When the Wu army was defeated, Guan Fu became famous all over the world.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Guan Fu charged into enemy lines during the rebellion.
evidence: Guan Fu put on his armor and held a halberd in his hand, and summoned dozens of warriors in the army who had always been friendly with him and were willing to go with him. After walking out of the military gate, no one dared to move forward. Only the two of them and Guan Fu's slaves, a total of more than ten cavalry, rushed into the Wu army until they reached the Wu army's general flag, killing and wounding dozens of enemy soldiers.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Guan Fu became a governor.
evidence: During the reign of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Guan Fuguan became the Prime Minister of the country.

Emperor Jing passed away and Emperor Wu, the current emperor, had just ascended the throne. He believed that Huaiyang was the transportation hub of the world and must be defended by strong troops, so he appointed Guan Fu as the governor of Huaiyang.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Guan Fu was dismissed for legal violations.
evidence: A few months later, he lost his official position because of a violation of the law.
A few years later, he was disgraced for breaking the law and lived idle at home in Chang'an.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Guan Fu was known for his straightforwardness.
evidence: Guan Fu is a strong and straightforward person, he is prone to drunkenness and does not like to flatter people in person.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Guan Fu was generous to the poor.
evidence: for many scholars who were below him, the poorer he was, the more respectful he was and treated them as equals.
In public, it is recommended to praise those who are lower than yourself.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Guan Fu disdained the powerful.
evidence: Guan Fu is a strong and straightforward person, he is prone to drunkenness and does not like to flatter people in person. For the emperor's relatives and powerful people, who were above him, he not only did not want to show respect to them, but also tried to find ways to insult them;
details.label: supported

details.claim: Guan Fu accumulated wealth.
evidence: The assets accumulated in his family are tens of millions, and the number of diners every day ranges from dozens to nearly a hundred.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Guan Fu became tyrannical in Yingchuan.
evidence: In order to build embankments and ponds in the countryside and irrigate farmland, his clan and guests expanded their power, monopolized interests, and became tyrannical in the Yingchuan area.
The children of Yingchuan then sang: If the Yingshui is clear, the Guan family will be at peace; if the Yingshui is turbid, the Guan family will be exterminated.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: After losing power, Guan Fu befriended Dou Ying.
evidence: When Wei Qihou lost power, he also wanted to follow Guan Fu to take revenge on those who usually admired him but abandoned him after losing power.
Guan Fu also wanted to follow Wei Qihou to make friends with other princes and the royal family to improve his reputation.
The two quoted each other and their relationship was as close as that between father and son.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Dou Ying and Guan Fu supported each other.
evidence: Wei Qihou lost power, he also wanted to follow Guan Fu to take revenge on those who usually admired him but abandoned him after losing power. Guan Fu also wanted to follow Wei Qihou to make friends with other princes and the royal family to improve his reputation. The two quoted each other and their relationship was as close as that between father and son.
Wei Qihou visited Guan Fu and planned to go with him.
Wei Qihou stepped forward to rescue Guan Fu.
Wei Qihou said: I earned the title of Marquis, and now I throw it away. There is nothing to regret. Besides, I can't let Guan Zhongru die on his own while I live alone.
The two protected each other, which caused this disaster.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Tian Fen once promised to visit Dou Ying.
evidence: Guanfu went to visit the Prime Minister during the period of mourning. The Prime Minister said casually: "I want to go with you to visit Wei Qihou. It just happens that you are in mourning and it is inconvenient to go." Guanfu said: "You are actually willing to come to Wei Qihou. How dare I, Guanfu, refuse because of mourning?" Please allow me to tell Wei Qihou to set up the curtains and prepare a banquet. You can come early tomorrow. Marquis Wu'an agreed.

Guan Fu told Wei Qihou in detail, just like he told Wu'an Hou. Wei Qihou and his wife specially bought more meat and wine, cleaned the house all night, arranged the curtains, and prepared the banquet. They were busy until dawn. As soon as it dawned, the people in charge of the mansion were asked to wait in front of the house. By noon, the prime minister had not arrived.
The Prime Minister only agreed to Guan Fu as a joke the day before, and really had no intention of coming to the banquet.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen failed to show for the visit.
evidence: By noon, the prime minister had not arrived.
The Prime Minister only agreed to Guan Fu as a joke the day before, and really had no intention of coming to the banquet.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Guan Fu confronted Tian Fen about the missed visit.
evidence: Guanfu went to visit the Prime Minister during the period of mourning. The Prime Minister said casually: "I want to go with you to visit Wei Qihou. It just happens that you are in mourning and it is inconvenient to go." Guanfu said: "You are actually willing to come to Wei Qihou. How dare I, Guanfu, refuse because of mourning?" Please allow me to tell Wei Qihou to set up the curtains and prepare a banquet. You can come early tomorrow. Marquis Wu'an agreed.

Guan Fu told Wei Qihou in detail, just like he told Wu'an Hou. Wei Qihou and his wife specially bought more meat and wine, cleaned the house all night, arranged the curtains, and prepared the banquet. They were busy until dawn. As soon as it dawned, the people in charge of the mansion were asked to wait in front of the house. By noon, the prime minister had not arrived. Wei Qihou said to Guan Fu: Has the Prime Minister forgotten this? Guanfu was very unhappy and said, "I, Guanfu, don't mind being in mourning, so I agreed to his appointment and he should come." So he drove and went to meet the prime minister in person.

The Prime Minister only agreed to Guan Fu as a joke the day before, and really had no intention of coming to the banquet. When Guan Fu came to the door, the prime minister was still sleeping. So Guan Fu went in to see him and said, "General, I was fortunate enough to pay a visit to Wei Qihou yesterday. Wei Qihou and his wife prepared wine and food, but they have not dared to eat anything from morning until now." Marquis Wu'an pretended to be surprised and apologized, saying: I was drunk yesterday and forgot what I said to you. So he drove there, but he went very slowly, which made Guan Fu even more angry.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen sought to seize Dou Ying's land.
evidence: The prime minister once sent Ji Fu to claim Wei Qihou's fields in the south of the city.
Wei Qihou said with great resentment: Although I have been abandoned and the general is noble, how can he take my land by force?

Soon, Wu'anhou heard that Wei Qihou and Guanfu were actually angry and refused to give up the land. He also said angrily: Wei Qihou's son once killed someone, and I saved his life. When I serve Wei Qihou, I always obey him. Why is he reluctant to part with these few hectares of fields?
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: The land dispute led to a feud between Tian Fen and Dou Ying.
evidence: The prime minister once sent Ji Fu to claim Wei Qihou's fields in the south of the city.
Wei Qihou said with great resentment: Although I have been abandoned and the general is noble, how can he take my land by force?
Soon, Wu'anhou heard that Wei Qihou and Guanfu were actually angry and refused to give up the land. He also said angrily: ... Why is he reluctant to part with these few hectares of fields?
From then on, Marquis Wu'an resented Guan Fu and Wei Qihou.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Tian Fen accused Guan Fu of tyranny.
evidence: Guan Fu's family lived in Yingchuan and were very rampant, and the people suffered from it.
Guan Fu made friends with powerful cunning people, oppressed the common people, accumulated tens of millions of wealth, ran rampant in Yingchuan, insulted and invaded the royal family.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Guan Fu retaliated by exposing Tian Fen's corruption.
evidence: Guan Fu also caught the Prime Minister's secrets, used illegal means to seek benefits, accepted money from King Huainan and said some things that he shouldn't have said.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: At a banquet, Guan Fu insulted Tian Fen.
evidence: Guanfu made fun of him during the banquet.
Guanfu got angry, so he smiled bitterly and said: "You are a noble man, I will entrust this cup to you!"

Guanfu had no place to vent his anger, so he scolded Marquis Linru and said: "Normally slandering Cheng Bushi is worthless. Today, the elders are toasting you for your birthday, but you are just like a girl, talking to Cheng Bushi."
Guanfu said, "I don't care if I kill my head or pierce my chest today. Why do I care about General Cheng and General Li!"
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Tian Fen had Guan Fu arrested.
evidence: Marquis Wu'an then ordered the knights to tie up Guan Fu and put him in the guest room.

He called Chang Shi and said, "Today we invite guests from the clan to the banquet. This is because of the Queen Mother's order." Guan Fu was impeached, saying that he insulted the guests at the banquet, insulted the edict, and committed the crime of "disrespect". He was imprisoned in a special prison.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Tian Fen charged Guan Fu with disrespect.
evidence: Guan Fu was impeached, saying that he insulted the guests at the banquet, insulted the edict, and committed the crime of 'disrespect'.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Dou Ying tried to save Guan Fu.
evidence: Wei Qihou stepped forward to rescue Guan Fu.
So he went out privately to write to the emperor without telling his family.

The emperor immediately called him into the palace, and Wei Qihou explained in detail the situation in which Guan Fu had lost his speech because he was drunk, and considered it not enough to sentence him to death.
Wei Qihou went to the East Palace and praised Guan Fu's merits, saying that he was guilty of drunkenness, but the prime minister used other crimes to frame Guan Fu.
Wei Qihou asked his nephew to write a letter to the emperor to report the acceptance of the imperial edict, hoping to be summoned by the emperor again.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Dou Ying failed to save Guan Fu.
evidence: Wei Qihou stepped forward to rescue Guan Fu.
Wei Qihou went to the East Palace and praised Guan Fu's merits, saying that he was guilty of drunkenness, but the prime minister used other crimes to frame Guan Fu.
Wei Qihou asked his nephew to write a letter to the emperor to report the acceptance of the imperial edict, hoping to be summoned by the emperor again.
It took a long time for Wei Qihou to hear the news. After hearing this, he was extremely angry and suffered from a stroke. He stopped eating and planned to die.
on the last day of December of that year, Wei Qihou was beheaded on the streets of Weicheng.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Tian Fen slandered Dou Ying.
evidence: Marquis Wu'an then tried his best to slander Guan Fu's arrogance and indulgence, and committed the crime of treason.
Wei Qihou thought that there was no other way to deal with it, so he attacked the prime minister's shortcomings.

Marquis Wu'an said: ... They are not like Wei Qihou and Guan Fu, who gathered the heroes of the world to discuss and discuss day and night. They secretly slandered and harbored deep dissatisfaction with the imperial court.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Dou Ying was imprisoned.
evidence: He was impeached and imprisoned in a special prison called Dusikong.
When he was imprisoned and Guan Fu was convicted of genocide, the situation became more and more urgent day by day.
Wei Qihou asked his nephew to write a letter to the emperor to report the acceptance of the imperial edict, hoping to be summoned by the emperor again.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Dou Ying claimed to have an imperial edict from Emperor Jing.
evidence: During the reign of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Wei Qihou received his edict before his death, which read: If something inconvenient happens to you, you can adapt to the situation and report your opinions to the emperor.
Wei Qihou asked his nephew to write a letter to the emperor to report the acceptance of the imperial edict, hoping to be summoned by the emperor again.
The memorial was submitted to the emperor, but after checking the files kept by the minister, there was no final edict from Emperor Jing.
This edict was only sealed and hidden in Wei Qihou's home, and was sealed by Wei Qihou's retainers.
Therefore, Wei Qihou was impeached for forging the imperial edict of the late emperor and should be sentenced to beheading in public.
details.label: supported

details.claim: The imperial edict was not found in records.
evidence: The memorial was submitted to the emperor, but after checking the files kept by the minister, there was no final edict from Emperor Jing.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Dou Ying was executed for forgery.
evidence: Wei Qihou asked his nephew to write a letter to the emperor to report the acceptance of the imperial edict, hoping to be summoned by the emperor again. The memorial was submitted to the emperor, but after checking the files kept by the minister, there was no final edict from Emperor Jing. This edict was only sealed and hidden in Wei Qihou's home, and was sealed by Wei Qihou's retainers. Therefore, Wei Qihou was impeached for forging the imperial edict of the late emperor and should be sentenced to beheading in public.

In October of the fifth year of Yuanguang, Guan Fu and his family were all executed. It took a long time for Wei Qihou to hear the news. After hearing this, he was extremely angry and suffered from a stroke. He stopped eating and planned to die. Someone heard that the emperor had no intention of killing Wei Qihou. Wei Qihou began to eat again, began to treat diseases, and discussed and decided not to impose the death penalty. There were rumors and many slanderous words about Wei Qihou were heard by the emperor, so on the last day of December of that year, Wei Qihou was beheaded on the streets of Weicheng.
details.label: unsupported

details.claim: Guan Fu and his family were executed.
evidence: In October of the fifth year of Yuanguang, Guan Fu and his family were all executed.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Tian Fen later fell ill.
evidence: In the spring of this year, Marquis Wu'an fell ill and kept shouting, saying things like apology.
He asked a wizard who could see ghosts to diagnose his illness. The wizard saw the ghosts of Wei Qihou and Guan Fu guarding Wu'anhou and wanted to kill him.
Finally died.

evidence: Zhao Sheng, Lord of Pingyuan, was a young master of the State of Zhao.
Among the many princes, Zhao Sheng was the most virtuous and talented.

evidence: He was hospitable and cultivated scholars. There were about thousands of guests who came to his sect.

evidence: Lord Pingyuan served as the prime minister of King Zhao Huiwen and King Xiaocheng.

evidence: He left the position of prime minister three times and was reinstated three times.
details.label: supported

evidence: His fiefdom was in Dongwu City.

evidence: There was a lame man in the house who always limped out to fetch water.
A beautiful concubine of Mr. Pingyuan lived upstairs. One day she looked down and saw the lame man fetching water, and she burst out laughing.

evidence: I wanted to get the head of the person who laughed at me.
details.label: unsupported

evidence: Mr. Pingyuan smiled and replied: "Okay." After the lame man left, Lord Pingyuan smiled again and said: Look at this boy, he wants to kill my concubine just because of a smile. Isn't it too much? I didn't kill that person after all.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Many scholars left Lord Pingyuan because of his refusal.

details.claim: When Qin besieged Handan, Lord Pingyuan sought help from Chu to form an alliance.
evidence: When the Qin State besieged Handan, King Zhao sent Lord Pingyuan to ask for help. At that time, he planned to recommend Chu as the leader of the alliance and make a joint alliance to fight against Qin.
Lord Pingyuan agreed to go to Chu State with twenty of his followers who were brave, resourceful, and capable of both civil and military affairs.

evidence: In the end, nineteen people were selected, and there was nothing left to choose from. There was no way to gather twenty people.
details.label: supported

details.claim: Mao Sui, a retainer for three years, volunteered.
evidence: At this time, a man named Mao Sui among the diners walked up to the front and recommended himself to Lord Pingyuan: I heard that you are going to Chu State, and let Chu State be the leader of the alliance to make an alliance. You also agreed to go with twenty diners, and no one will go outside to search. There is still one person missing now, I hope you can use me to recharge and go together.
Mr. Pingyuan asked: How many years has it been since Mr. Wang stayed with me? Mao Sui replied: It has been three years now.

evidence: Mr. Pingyuan said: A talented wise man living in the world is like an awl placed in a pocket, its sharp edge will be revealed immediately. This is because your husband has no expertise. Sir, you can't go. Sir, please stay.

details.claim: In Chu, negotiations stalled until Mao Sui confronted the King of Chu.

So Mao Sui gripped the hilt of his sword tightly, trotted all the way up the steps to the palace, and said to Lord Pingyuan: Talking about cooperation is either beneficial or harmful, just two sentences. Now we have been talking about the marriage since the morning, but by noon we still can’t decide. What’s the reason?

details.claim: Mao Sui sealed the alliance with a blood oath.
evidence: Mao Sui knelt down with the copper plate in his hands, presented it to the King of Chu and said: Your Majesty, you should suck the blood first to show your sincerity in confirming the alliance. The next one is my master, and the next one is me.
In this way, the alliance alliance was confirmed in the palace of Chu State.

Yu Qing replied: Zhao Hao said that if Qin doesn't make peace, next year Qin will attack the king again. Wouldn't the king want to cede his hinterland to it to seek peace? details.claim: Tai Shigong reflects on Mencius.
evidence: Tai Shigong said: When I read "Mencius", whenever I read that King Hui of Liang asked how to make profits for our country, I couldn't help but put down the book and sigh.
Said: Alas, seeking profit is really the beginning of all troubles!
Confucius rarely talked about the issue of profit. The reason was that he wanted to fundamentally prevent this source of trouble.
So he said that acting based on personal interests will lead to a lot of resentment.
From the emperor down to the common people, the disadvantages of being greedy for profit exist. What's the difference?

details.claim: As chaos spread across the empire, Liu Xiu pacified various rebel groups.

details.claim: Liu Xiu pacified the Bronze Horse Army.

After more than a month of this, the Bronze Horse Army ran out of food and fled in the middle of the night. Guangwu led his army to pursue them to Guantao County and defeated the Bronze Horse Army.

Before all the Bronze Horse Army surrendered, Gaohu and Chonglian came from the southeast to join the remaining Bronze Horse Army. Guangwu then fought fiercely with them in Puyang, defeated the enemy forces across the board and made them surrender, and named their generals as marquises.

details.claim: Wei Qing's nephew Huo Qubing emerged as a brilliant commander.
evidence: This year, Huo Qubing, the son of General Wei Qing's sister, was eighteen years old. He was favored by Emperor Wu and became the emperor's servant.

Huo Qubing was good at horseback riding and archery. He accompanied the general on two expeditions. The general, on the emperor's order, allocated some brave warriors to him and appointed him as the captain of Gaoyao. He and 800 light and brave cavalry left the army for hundreds of miles, looking for favorable opportunities to attack and kill the enemy. The number of enemy soldiers they killed exceeded their losses.

So the emperor said: Huo Qubing, the lieutenant of the Yao School, killed 2,028 enemies, including the Xiongnu Prime Minister and the household. He killed Shanyu's grandfather's Ji Ruohou Chan, and captured Shanyu's uncle Luo Gubi alive. For his merits, he twice won the first place in the army, and designated 1,600 households to confer Huo Qubing as the champion marquis.

The champion Hou Huo Qubing was granted the title of Marquis for three years. In the spring of the second year of Yuanshou, the emperor appointed the champion Hou Huo Qubing as a general of hussars, leading 10,000 cavalry to attack the Xiongnu from Longxi and achieving military merit.
In total, Hussar General Huo Qubing made six sorties against the Huns, four of which were as generals, and killed more than 110,000 Huns.
details.label: supported

The hussar generals lead soldiers who are often selected. However, he dared to fight deep into the enemy's territory and often ran in front of the army with his strong cavalry.

The hussar general also led 50,000 cavalry and carried the same military supplies as the general Wei Qing, but he had no lieutenants. He appointed Li Gan and others as senior colonels and deputy generals, and sent troops from Daijun and Youbeiping for more than a thousand miles.

General Huo Qubing led the army to the expedition, and personally led the captured Xiongnu soldiers, carrying a small amount of military supplies, across the desert, crossed the river to capture the Shanyu's close minister Zhangqu, killed the little Xiongnu king Bicheqi, and then attacked the Xiongnu general Zuo, beheaded the enemy general, and seized his flag and war drum. After crossing Lihou Mountain and crossing the Gonglu River, they captured three Xiongnu soldiers, including the King of Tuntou and the King of Han, as well as eighty-three people including generals, prime ministers, danghu, and captains. Then they worshiped heaven at Langjuxu Mountain, worshiped earth at Guyan Mountain, and climbed high mountains to look at the desert.

details.claim: The text details the perils of lobbying.
evidence: Generally speaking, the difficulty in lobbying is not that my intelligence is not enough to persuade the monarch; nor is it that my eloquence is not enough to clearly express my thoughts; nor is it that I dare not express all my opinions without hesitation. In general lobbying, the difficulty lies in how to understand the psychology of the target of lobbying and then use my words to satisfy his wishes.

If the person you are lobbying intends to gain a high reputation, but the lobbyist uses heavy profits to persuade him, the other party will think that you have low moral character and will be treated despicably. You will definitely be abandoned and alienated.

If the target of the lobbying is greedy for huge profits, but the lobbyist uses the idea of ​​gaining high reputation to persuade him, he will think that you have no brains and are divorced from reality, and he will definitely not accept your opinions.
If the monarch makes a mistake, but the lobbyist cites some good arguments to deduce the seriousness of his fault, then the lobbyist will be in danger.
I only lament that Han Fei wrote "Shuo Nan" but he could not escape the disaster of lobbying the monarch.

details.claim: The text uses historical anecdotes to illustrate points.

Once upon a time, Duke Wu of Zheng wanted to attack the State of Hu, but instead gave his daughter to the monarch of the State of Hu. He asked the ministers: If I want to use troops, who can I attack? Guan Qisi replied: We can attack Hu. Duke Wu of Zheng killed Guan Qisi and said, "The State of Hu is the country of our brothers. What do you mean by attacking it?" When the king of Hu heard about this, he thought the king of Zheng was his relative and did not guard against him. Zheng took the opportunity to attack Hu and occupied it.

Once upon a time, Mi Zixia was favored by the monarch of the Wei Kingdom. According to the laws of Weiguo, anyone who secretly drives your car must have his or her feet cut off. Soon, Mi Zixia's mother fell ill. Someone knew about it and informed him overnight. Mi Zixia pretended to be the Lord's order and drove out in the King's car. When the monarch heard about this, he praised him and said: How filial you are, you are willing to commit the punishment of amputating your feet because of your mother's illness! Mi Zixia and Wei Jun went to the orchard to play. Mi Zixia ate a sweet peach and offered it to Wei Jun before finishing it. Wei Jun said: You really love me, you don’t eat but you think about me! When Mizi's beauty faded, Lord Wei's love for him also faded away, and he later offended Lord Wei. Wei Jun said: This man once pretended to be my order to drive my car, and he also gave me the leftover peach to eat.

Lu Zhonglian said: The world thinks that Bao Jiao committed suicide because of his narrow-mindedness. This view is completely wrong. details.claim: Xiangru advised the emperor against dangerous hunting.

Although it is absolutely safe and harmless, this is not a place that the emperor should approach. What's more, it is very easy to trek through the basil and run on the ruins of barren hills. There is the joy of hunting wild beasts in front of you, but you are not prepared to deal with sudden accidents in your heart. It is probably very easy for disaster to occur. As for belittling the king's noble status, not taking it as a comfort, but willing to appear in a place that is still slightly dangerous despite being fully prepared, I personally think that your majesty should not do this. Perhaps those who are discerning can see the occurrence of something long before it happens, and those who are wise can avoid it before the disaster occurs. Most disasters are hidden in secret places and occur when people are careless. Therefore, the proverb says: If you accumulate thousands of gold at home, you will not sit under the eaves of the hall. He left the piano player and pressed his sword and said, "Sir, you only see my appearance and haven't observed me carefully. How can you know that I am playing well?" Zou Jizi said: The big string is slow and gentle, which symbolizes the king; the small string is high-pitched, bright and clear, symbolizing the prime minister; the fingers are pulling the string hard and letting it go slowly, symbolizing the government order; the sound of the piano is harmonious, the large and small are coordinated beautifully, and the twists and turns do not interfere with each other, symbolizing the four seasons: I can know how well you play from this. If it is to govern the country and appease the people, how can it be among the strings? details.claim: He advised Emperor Shun against drawing lots to choose a queen.
evidence: Emperor Shun wanted to make a queen, but among the nobles there were four favored ones. He didn't know who to make, so he decided to draw lots and ask God to choose the queen. Hu Guang, together with Shangshu Guo Qian and Shi Chang, went to the court to remonstrate: I saw the imperial edict privately and thought that establishing a queen was a major event. I was humble and refused to make my own decision. I wanted to use the method of drawing lots to ask God to resolve the doubts. There are no ancestral allusions recorded in ancient books. Relying on gods and witches may not necessarily find wise men, but even if you meet such people, you are not choosing people based on virtue. Human appearance comes from nature, so there must be different appearances in heaven. We should refer to good families and choose virtuous people. If they have the same virtues, they should look at their age. If they are equal in age, they should look at their appearance. They should consider the classics and judge from the saints. Government orders are like sweating. Once they come out, they cannot be taken back. Once the edict was issued, it was seen everywhere. The minister's duty is to collect lost things, and he is deeply concerned about the responsibility, so he is anxious and ventures to state his opinions. The emperor obeyed and appointed Liang Guiren, a woman from a good family, as his queen.

Yuan An's nephew Yuan Zhong served as an attendant knight, guarding the emperor with talismans. Yuan Zhong persuaded Yuan Ang: "Fight with him and insult him in the court, so that his slanderous words will have no effect."

Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty went on a tour, and Zhao Tong accompanied him in the car. Yuan Ang lay in front of the car and said: I heard that the people who accompany the emperor on the tall chariot are all heroes in the world. Although the Han Dynasty lacks talents today, why does Your Majesty only want to ride in the same carriage with people who have been cut by swords and saws? It is human beings who can explain the common sense of things thoroughly and understand it from the heart and be able to analyze it. It is unreasonable to exclude people and use the law exclusively. Nowadays, the quality of the imperial examination is not as good as appointing prominent officials to evaluate the people under their jurisdiction. After serving for one year, the outstanding person will be selected as the superior person every year, and the poor person will be classified as the inferior person. Nowadays, the evaluation of political performance is indeed divided into difficulties and difficulties because of the different conditions for holding the position. Zhang Huan and others went to Tingwei to be prisoners. It took several days to get out, and they used three months' salary to atone for their sins.

When Zhang Huan was the general of the Liao Dynasty, he and Duan Yin fought against each other to attack the Qiang people, and there was no harmony.
When Duan Yin was the captain of Sili school, he wanted to drive Zhang Huan back to Dunhuang and frame him.

He was a hairless man, but wanted to be used by others. This was why Chunyu Kun patted his thighs and looked up to the sky, laughing.
I really know that what I say will definitely be ridiculed by you, but I still put my hope in it. Why?

Isn’t the virtue of Dang Tong, King Wen, and King Yan Zhao great?
It is common sense for ordinary people to cry out to Heaven when they are wronged, and to hammer their hearts out when they are in poverty.
Now it's useless to yell every day for no response. It's really hurting to the extreme.
You and I were both born in the holy world, and I was alone and ignored by others.
Lonely and humble, with no one to tell you.
If you don't pity me, I will become a fish.
Looking eastward, there is nothing else to say.
Although Duan Juan was a fierce man, after reading his letter, he felt pity for him and finally couldn't bear to harm him.
At that time, many dishonest people were imprisoned, some were executed, and some were relocated.
Zhang Huan stayed behind closed doors, educated thousands of disciples, and wrote "The Difficulty of Shang Shu" with more than 300,000 words.
Zhang Huan was determined and disciplined when he was young. I once said to my friends: A real man should make contributions to the country.

The will said: I have been an official before and after, and I want silver moxa. I can't join in the evil, and I will be jealous of the bad guys.

But there is darkness under the ground, and there is never any dawn, but the coffin is wrapped in silk and nails are densely hammered on it. This is what I don't like.
We have prepared caves before, which is good. If he died in the morning, he would bury it in the evening, put the body on the bier, and cover it with a scarf.
If you are extravagant and don’t learn Jin literature, if you are frugal you don’t learn from the kings and grandsons, if you follow your destiny and love, you will hardly have any guilt.
Several sons followed his will.
Most of Wuwei's temples were erected, and sacrifices were made continuously from generation to generation.
He wrote twenty-four inscriptions, odes, books, teachings, commandments, aspirations, countermeasures, and chapters.
The eldest son Zhang Zhi, whose courtesy name is Boying, is the most famous. Zhang Zhi and his younger brother Zhang Chang, whose courtesy name is Wenshu, are both good at cursive calligraphy and are praised today.
At first, Zhang Huan was appointed as the prefect of Wuwei. His wife was pregnant. She dreamed of going upstairs to sing with Zhang Huan's seal and ribbon. She asked the person who predicted the dream, "I will definitely give birth to a boy, and he will guard this country and die in this building."
Later, Zhang Meng was born, and he served as the prefect of Wuwei in Jian'an. He killed Handan merchants, the governor, and state soldiers surrounded him.
Historian comments: Since the eunuch Zheng Zhong was granted the title of Marquis of Chaoxiang, the eunuchs have wielded power for generations and caused harm for decades. There is no one in the four seas who does not hate him with gnashing of teeth and hopes to eliminate his species.
Chen Fan and Dou Wu rose up to make plans and called on the world. This is known to all celebrities and knowledgeable people.
