"Poetry" says: Tears are streaming down his face!
It’s too late to lament!
◆The biography of Duan Jiong, whose courtesy name is Ji Ming, was from Guzang County, Wuwei County. His ancestors came from Duan Jiong, uncle of Zheng Gong.
He is the great-grandson of the Western Region Protector Huizong.
Duan Juan learned horse racing and archery when he was young. He liked knight-errants and took bribes lightly. When he grew up, he changed his youthful ambition and became interested in ancient learning.
He was initially elected as Xiaolian and served as Xianlingyuan Cheng and Yangling Ling. He showed great talents in office.
When he was promoted to captain of the Liaodong vassal state, Xianbei invaded the frontier fortress, so Duan Jun led his troops to the frontier fortress.
Because he was afraid that the thieves would flee in fear, he sent a post rider to pretend to deliver a seal to order Duan Jiong to retreat. Duan Jiong pretended to retreat on the road and set up an ambush on the retreating road.
Xianbei thought that Duan Jiong was really retreating and pursued Duan Jiong.
Duan Qiao then sent out a large number of troops, and all the Xianbei invaders were captured.
Duan Jong, however, deserved severe punishment for falsely claiming to be the official seal official. Because of his meritorious service, he was punished as a bandit and sent to the border to defend against enemies.
After serving his sentence, he was appointed as Yilang.
At this time, Taishan, Langfu bandits Dongguo Dou, Gongsun Ju and others gathered 30,000 people and destroyed the counties. The imperial court sent troops to suppress the rebellion, which could not be quelled for several years.
In the second year of Yongshou's reign, Emperor Huan ordered the ministers to elect those with all-round talents in both civil and military affairs as generals. Situ Yin Song recommended Duan Jiong, and Duan Jiong was awarded the title of Zhonglang General.
He conquered Dongguo Dou, Gongsun Ju and others and won a great victory. He killed Dongguo Dou and Gongsun Ju and gained more than 10,000 leaders. Some of the remaining party members fled and some surrendered.
He made Duanju a prince, rewarded him with 500,000 yuan, and appointed one of his sons as a doctor.
In the second year of Yanxi's reign, he was promoted to the rank of Colonel Protecting Qiang.
When eight kinds of Qiang including Shaodang, Shaohe, Dangjian and Lejie invaded the borders of Longxi and Jincheng, Duan Jun led his troops and 12,000 Huangzhong uprising Qiang cavalry out of Huanggu and defeated them.
Pursuing the remaining troops who fled south across the Yellow River, they sent military officials Tian Yan and Xia Yu to recruit warriors to ascend first and use ropes to pull them up. They then fought at Luoting and won a great victory. They killed 2,000 people under their leader and captured more than 10,000 people. The remaining captives fled.
In the spring of the second year, the remaining Qiang captives and Marshal Shao He invaded Zhangye, captured Juluwu, and killed the officials and people of the country. They also summoned more than a thousand tribesmen of their own kind and concentrated their forces to attack Duan Jiong's troops at dawn.
Duan Jiong dismounted and fought with them. The battle lasted until noon, when all the swords and arrows were broken and the prisoners retreated.
Duan Jiao pursued, fighting and walking at the same time, fighting day and night, cutting flesh and swallowing snow. After more than forty days, they arrived at Jishi Mountain, the source of the Yellow River, and traveled more than 2,000 miles beyond the Great Wall. They beheaded and burned Marshal He, and killed and captured more than 5,000 people.
They also divided their troops to attack the Shicheng Qiang and killed 1,600 people who drowned.
More than ninety people from Shaodangzhong surrendered to Duan Jiong.
When the Qiang hybrids were stationed in Baishi, Duan Jong sent troops to attack, beheading and capturing more than 3,000 people.
In winter, Le Jie and Ling Wuzhong surrounded Yunjie, killing and robbing officials and people. Duan Juan organized a rescue camp and captured hundreds of people.
In the winter of the fourth year, Shen Di, Longxi Laojie, and Wuwu Qiang from Shangjun jointly invaded the two prefectures of Bing and Liang. Duan Jun led the Qiang uprising in Huangzhong to conquer them.
Guo Hong, the governor of Liangzhou, shared the military exploits with Duan Jiong and delayed and stopped Duan Jiong's army from advancing.
The uprising Qiang had been fighting for too long and missed their hometown, so they all rebelled.
Guo Hong put the blame on Duan Jiong, who was therefore arrested and imprisoned and sentenced to hard labor.
The Qiang pirates became more rampant, captured camps, and colluded with each other to disrupt various counties. So thousands of officials and people stayed at the court to appeal to Duan Jiong.
The imperial court knew that Duan Jiong had been framed by Guo Hong, and the emperor issued an edict to inquire about Duan Jiong's situation.
Duan Jiong just apologized and did not dare to say that he had been wronged. The capital called Duan Jiong an elder.
He was transferred from among the criminals, appointed as Yilang, and promoted to governor of Bingzhou.
At that time, five or six thousand Qiang people from Dian and other tribes invaded Wuwei, Zhangye, and Jiuquan and burned people's houses.
In six years, the enemy forces became stronger and Liangzhou almost fell.
In the winter, Duan Ji was appointed as the captain of the Qiang Guard, and he rushed to his post by post.
In the spring of the next year, 355 Qiang marshals including Fengshuang, Liangduo, and Dianna led 3,000 tribesmen and surrendered in front of Duan Jiao's army.
Dangjian and Lejiezhong also gathered and stationed themselves.
In winter, Duan Juan defeated them with more than 10,000 people, beheaded their commander, and killed more than 4,000 prisoners.
In the spring of the eighth year, Duan Juan attacked Lejiezhong again, beheading more than 400 people and surrendering more than 2,000 people.
In the summer, they marched to attack Dang Jianzhong in Huangzhong. Duan Zhao's soldiers were defeated and were besieged for three days. He used the hermit Fan Zhi to devise a strategy and secretly sent out troops at night, beating drums to fight back. They defeated the rebel army and killed thousands of people.
Duan Jiong pursued them fiercely, moving through the valleys, fighting every day from spring to autumn. As a result, the enemy was hungry and sleepy, so they fled and went north to invade the Wuwei area.
Duan Juan defeated the Xiqiang, beheading 23,000 people in total, captured tens of thousands of people, and captured 8 million horses, cattle and sheep. More than 10,000 tribesmen surrendered.
He was granted the title of Marquis of Duanjudu Township, with a settlement of 500 households.
In the first year of Yongkang, Dangjian Zhuzhong rebelled and gathered more than 4,000 people to attack Wuwei. Duan Jiong pursued Luanniao and completely defeated them. He killed their leader and beheaded more than 3,000 people. The Xiqiang was pacified from then on.
Since the Eastern Qiang Xianling and others defeated the general Ma Xian who conquered the West, the imperial court was unable to conquer and often harassed the three assistants.
Later, the Liao generals Huangfu Gui and Zhonglang general Zhang Huan tried to surrender year after year, but they always surrendered and then rebelled.
Emperor Huan issued an edict and asked Duan Qiang: "Xian Ling Dong Qiang rebelled against evil, but Huangfu Gui and Zhang Huan each had elite troops and could not quell them on time."
I want you to lead an army to conquer the east, but I don't know what is appropriate. Can you come up with some strategies?
Duan Jiong said: I saw that although the Xianling Dongqiang rebelled many times, about 20,000 tribesmen had surrendered to Huangfu Gui. Who is good and who is evil has been distinguished, and there are not many bandits left.
Now Zhang Huan is delaying to advance, probably because he is afraid that the enemy will separate from the outside and unite with the inside. If he sends troops to go there, those who surrender will be frightened.
Moreover, they have been gathering and stationed from winter to spring. The men and horses are tired and sick. This is a suicidal situation. As long as they recruit surrender quickly, they can subdue the powerful enemy without sending a single soldier.
I think the ambition of a wolf is not easy to be met with kindness. When they are cornered, they may surrender, but once they withdraw their troops, they will become riotous again.
The only way to scare them is to use a spear with a white blade on their necks!
It is estimated that there are more than 30,000 tribes left in Dongzhong, which are close to the fortress. The roads are flat and there is no situation where Yan, Qi, Qin, and Zhao are in the same position. However, they have harassed Bingzhou and Liangzhou for a long time, and have repeatedly invaded Sanfu, Xihe, and Shangjun. This is like a hidden cancer that stays under the side of the body. If it is not eliminated, it will soon grow bigger.
Now if we use 5,000 cavalry, 10,000 infantry, and 3,000 chariots, we can completely defeat them and pacify them in two or three years, and we don't have to worry about the cost of 5.4 billion.
In this way, the Qiang group can be defeated and the Xiongnu can be subdued. Those who moved to Sene County can return to their homeland.
I think in the early years of Yonghe, the Qiang rebelled, spending 24 billion for four years; at the end of Yonghe, after another seven years, more than 8 billion were spent.
After spending so much money and time, they still haven't killed them all. The remnants have reappeared and are causing harm to this day. If we don't temporarily tire the people, there will never be peace.
I am willing to use all my dull talents and wait for the fate to be dispatched.
The emperor praised him and fully listened to his words.
In the spring of the first year of Jianning, Duan Juan led more than 10,000 troops and carried fifteen days' worth of food and grass from Pengyang to Gaoping, where he fought with Xianling and others at Fengyi Mountain.
There were many captives, and Duan Jiong's troops became frightened.
Duan Jong ordered his troops to tighten their bowstrings, sharpen their swords and spears, use triple spears, carry strong crossbows, and deploy light cavalry on the left and right wings. He encouraged the generals and said: "Now that we are thousands of miles away from home, if we advance, our career will be successful; if we escape, we will die. Let's work together to gain fame!"
So with a loud shout, the army jumped into battle. Duan Jun was galloping beside him and suddenly attacked. The captive army collapsed. More than 8,000 soldiers were beheaded and 280,000 cattle, horses and sheep were captured.
At this time, Empress Dowager Dou came to power and issued an edict: "Xian Ling Dong Qiang has been causing harm for many years. Duan Qiang previously stated the situation and believed that it must be eradicated."
Duan Jiong walked in the frost and snow, marching quickly during the day and night. Being a target makes the warrior feel inspired.
In less than ten days, the enemy invaders fled and dispersed. Their bodies were connected and many were captured alive. The number of captives cannot be counted.
He has wiped away the hatred of defeat for a hundred years and comforted the soul of the loyal general. His contribution is remarkable, and I highly commend him.
When Dong Qiang is completely pacified, his meritorious deeds should be remembered together.
Now Duan is temporarily given 200,000 yuan and a member of his family is appointed as the doctor.
At the same time, the Zhongzang government was ordered to allocate money and gifts to increase military expenditures.
Appointed Duan Jiong as General Po Qiang.
In the summer, Duan Qiang pursued the Qiang out of the bridge gate and onto the Zouma River.
Soon, I heard the news that the bandits were captured in Sheyanze, so I led my brisk troops to advance quickly, covering more than 200 miles in a day and night. I caught up with the thieves in the morning and defeated them. The remaining bandits fled to Luochuan and gathered again.
Duan Yan then sent his cavalry commander Tian Yan to lead 5,000 men out to the east, fake Sima Xia Yu to lead 2,000 men around the west, and the Qiang sent 6 to 7,000 men to besiege Tian Yan and others. Tian Yan and others fought with the captives, and the captives broke up and fled.
Duan Yan rushed forward and pursued with Tian Yan and others on the Lingxianshui River.
Duan Jong's soldiers were hungry and thirsty, so he ordered his troops to advance together to seize the water, but the captives broke up and fled.
Duan Jiawei chased after him, and the prisoners fought and retreated until they reached Lingwu Valley.
Duan Yan took the lead in the battle wearing armor, and no soldier dared to stand still.
The Qiang captives were defeated and fled away, abandoning their weapons.
After three days and three nights of pursuit, the soldier's feet were covered with thick calluses.
After chasing to Jingyang, the remaining 4,000 tribesmen dispersed into the Hanyang Valley.
At this time, Zhang Huan said: Although the Eastern Qiang has been destroyed, the remaining species are not easy to eliminate. Duan Qiang is frivolous but courageous. He is worried that he will lose the battle and cannot guarantee permanent victory.
You should use kindness to persuade others to surrender, so that you will not regret it.
The edict was issued to Duan Jiong.
Duan Qiang went on to say: I originally knew that although the Dong Qiang had many soldiers, they were weak and easy to subdue, so I approached Chen Yu and thought of a plan for permanent peace.
However, Zhang Huan, the commander-in-chief, said that the enemy would not be easily defeated and should be surrendered.
The emperor's sage believed and accepted my unseen words, so that my plan could be realized and Zhang Huan's strategy was not used.
Facts have shown that, contrary to what Zhang Huan said, Zhang Huan harbored suspicion and hatred.
They believed the words of the rebellious Qiang, but modified their original meaning, saying that my soldiers were wounded and defeated many times, and that the Qiang were also born from the Qi of Bingtian and could not be killed. The valley was vast and could not be left alone. Blood flowed all over the field, hurting the harmony and bringing disaster.
I think that during the Zhou and Qin Dynasties, the Rong and Di were causing harm; since the rise of Guangwu, the Qiang bandits have become very powerful and cannot be killed. They have surrendered and then rebelled.
Now Xian zero bastards are capricious, conquering counties and cities, robbing people, digging graves and throwing corpses. Everyone, living or dead, suffers from their harm. God is angry and lends my hand to punish them.
Once upon a time, the country of Xing was unruly, and the defenders of the country attacked it. They sent out troops, and rain fell from the sky, which alleviated the drought. I marched through the hot summer, and received good rains one after another, and the harvests were abundant, and the people were free from diseases.
The higher one controls the heart of heaven and avoids disasters; the lower one observes human affairs and wins the hearts of the people, so he can win the battle.
From the west of Qiaomen to the east of Luochuan, the original government counties and cities were continuous. They were not in deep and dangerous areas. The chariots and cavalry could move safely without any casualties.
Zhang Huan was an official of the Han Dynasty. As an officer, he had been stationed in the army for two years. He was unable to quell the rebellion. He only wanted to cultivate literature and did not want to use force. He wanted to recruit ferocious enemies. His absurd and empty words were unreasonable.
Why do you say that?
In the past, when there were no border invaders, Zhao Chongguo moved them to the interior; when Jian Dang harassed the border, Ma Yuan moved them to Sanfu and initially submitted them, but in the end they rebelled and have caused harm to this day.
Therefore, people with far-sighted vision think this is the most worrying thing.
Nowadays, border counties have few households and have been repeatedly invaded by Qiang. Bandits who want to surrender live together with civilians. It is just like planting thorny tangerine trees and thorn trees in fertile fields or raising venomous snakes indoors. How dangerous it is!
Therefore, I followed the authority of the Han Dynasty and established a long-term strategy to cut off the roots and prevent them from reproducing and growing. The original planned cost of three years was 5.4 billion, but now it has only been one year and less than half has been spent. The remaining invaders have become remnants of flames and will be wiped out soon.
Every time I receive an edict, the army is outside and cannot be commanded from within. I hope that it will be exactly as this sentence says, and I will be responsible for it and adapt to the situation without losing expediency.
In the second year, the imperial edict sent an interviewer, Feng Chan, to persuade the scattered Qiang people in Hanyang to surrender.
Duan Jun believed that it was spring sowing time and the people were working in the fields. Although the Qiang temporarily surrendered and the government had no food, the Qiang captives would definitely become thieves again.
In the summer, Duan Jue himself entered the camp forty or fifty miles away from Fanting Mountain where the Qiang were stationed. He sent Tian Yan and Xia Yu to lead five thousand people to garrison the mountain.
The whole Qiang army attacked and asked sternly: "Are Tian Yan and Xia Yu here?"
Where are the Qiang who surrendered in Huangzhong?
Today we have to fight to the death.
The army was frightened, so Tian Yan and others encouraged the soldiers to fight desperately and defeated the Qiang captives.
The Qiang army broke up and fled eastward. They gathered in Shehu Valley and divided their troops to guard the upper and lower gates of each valley.
Duan Juan planned to eliminate them in one fell swoop and prevent them from escaping again, so he sent thousands of people to build a wooden fence in west County, twenty paces wide and forty miles long, to stop them.
Tian Yan and Xia Yu were assigned to lead 7,000 people to quietly go up to the Western Mountains at night and build a position about a mile away from the Qiang captives.
He also sent Sima Zhang Kai and others to lead 3,000 people to Dongshan.
The Qiang captives discovered this and attacked Tian Yan and others, blocking the water channels.
Duan Jue himself led the infantry and cavalry to attack the water.
The Qiang captives retreated, but because they, together with Zhang Kai and others, took Dongxi Mountain hostage and sent their troops to attack, the Qiang captives were defeated and dispersed.
Duan Jiong pursued him into the barren mountains and deep valleys at the upper and lower gates of the valley, defeating them everywhere. He killed 19,000 levels below his commander, and obtained innumerable oxen, horses, mules, donkeys, felt, fur, tents, tents, and other items.
The four thousand people recruited by Feng Chan were placed in Anding, Hanyang, and Longxi counties respectively. So far, all the Eastern Qiang were pacified.
A total of 180 battles were fought, more than 38,600 enemies were beheaded, more than 427,500 cattle, horses, sheep, mules, donkeys and camels were captured, at a cost of 4.4 billion, and more than 400 soldiers were killed.
Duan Jiong was granted the title of Marquis of Xinfeng County, with ten thousand households in the city.
Duan Yan marched with benevolence, and when his soldiers were sick, he personally expressed condolences and bandaged their wounds.
I have been on the border for more than ten years and have never had a good night's sleep.
He shares the joys and sorrows with the soldiers, so the soldiers are willing to fight to the death for him.
In the spring of the third year, he summoned back the capital and led more than 50,000 Qin and Hu infantry and cavalry, as well as thousands of horses with sweat and blood, and captured more than 10,000 people.
The emperor sent Dahong to show condolences to Hao.
When the troops arrived, Duan Jiong was granted the title of Shizhong. He was transferred to Jinwu and Henan Yin.
Some thieves excavated Feng Guiren's tomb, and after being convicted, he was demoted to an admonishing doctor, and then promoted to a lieutenant.
Duan Juan relied on the eunuchs, so he could keep his wealth and honor. He became a party member with Wang Fu, the official of the Zhongchang, and unjustly killed Zheng Sa, Dong Teng and others.
In the second year, he replaced Li Xian as Taiwei. In the winter of this year, he was dismissed due to illness and was appointed as Sili Xiaowei again.
A few years later, he was transferred to the prefect of Yingchuan and recruited as a doctor in Taizhong.
In the second year of Guanghe's reign, he replaced Qiao Xuan as Taiwei.
After reigning for more than a month, he impeached himself due to a solar eclipse. Officials reported him and ordered him to take away his seal and ribbon and send him to the court for trial.
At this time, Captain Yang Qiu of the Sili School ordered Wang Fu to be killed, which implicated Duan Jiong, so he was questioned and reprimanded in prison. Duan Jiong then committed suicide by committing poison, and his family members moved to the border.
Later, Lu Qiang, the general servant of the imperial court, came to Shu to pursue Duan Juan's achievements. Emperor Ling issued an edict to return Duan Juan's wife and children to the county.
In the past, Duan Juan, Huangfu Weiming and Zhang Ranming were all famous, and the capital was called "Liangzhou Sanming".

When the days come, it becomes a cycle. A saint who understands this principle will avoid disaster himself. When a wise king applies this principle, no one dares to deceive him. Therefore, the arrival of happiness is created by people themselves; the arrival of disaster is also caused by people themselves. Disaster and happiness coexist, punishment and reward complement each other. The sage understands this truth clearly and therefore knows the good and bad. During the reigns of Jie of Xia and Zhou of Shang, they competed with the heavens for merit and hindered ghosts and gods from communicating with each other. This is already cruel and unethical, and there are many flatterers. Xia Jie had a flattering minister named Zhao Liang. He instigated King Jie to be cruel and cruel, encouraged him to be as greedy as a wolf, imprisoned Shang Tang in Xiatai, and killed Guan Longfeng. The people on the left and right are afraid of being killed, and they are just trying to flatter themselves. The country is in danger, but everyone says it doesn't matter. They shouted long live happily, but confusedly said that the fate of the country was not over yet. Blind Xia Jie's ears and eyes, and join him in deceit and madness. Shang Tang finally defeated Xia Jie, and Xia Jie died. Xia Jie listened to Zhao Liang, a flattering official, and suffered disaster alone. "Spring and Autumn" recorded this incident, which is still unforgettable. During the Shang Dynasty, there was a flattering minister named Zuo Qiang. He boasted about his skillful eyes and instigated King Zhou to build an象廊. The象廊 is as high as the sky, and a jade bed is placed there. Utensils carved from rhinoceros horn and jade are used, and ivory chopsticks are used to eat. The heart of the sage Bigan was dug out, and the legs of the strong man were cut off. Jizi was afraid of being killed, so he let his hair down and pretended to be crazy. King Zhou killed Prince Li of Zhou and imprisoned King Wen of Zhou Jichang. Throw King Wen into a stone chamber and prepare to imprison him from night to dawn. Yin Jing rescued King Wen and escaped with him. King Wen entered the Zhou Dynasty and obtained Tai Gongwang. He mobilized his soldiers, gathered weapons, and fought against Shang Zhou. King Wen died of illness, and his subordinates carried his body forward. Prince Ji Fa replaced his father as a general, and his temple title was King Wu. King Wu and King Zhou fought in Muye and defeated the Zhou army south of Mount Huashan. King Zhou was defeated and fled back. King Wu besieged him in the象廊. King Zhou committed suicide in the Proclamation Chamber, but he was not allowed to be buried after his death. The head was hung on the beam of the cart and was pulled by four horses. When I think of King Zhou's situation, my heart is filled with sorrow like boiling water. These people are all rich and noble, but they are too arrogant. When desires are not satisfied, people tend to be ambitious, greedy and arrogant. If you do not appoint loyal and trustworthy people, but listen to those flattering ministers, you will eventually be ridiculed by the world. Now my territory is between the various vassal states, not even the slightest bit inferior to it. If you don't do things properly, how can you escape disaster!
